hook.line: You have already said it twice, and they ask again. In Spanish you can answer by repeating *que sí* or *que no*, with a little impatience in your voice. Tomás hears it from Hernando every morning.
hook.es: Que sí, mamá, que ya te llamo.
hook.en: Yes, Mom, I told you, I'll call you in a minute.

examples.es: Que sí, mamá, que ya te llamo.
examples.en: Yes, Mom, I told you, I'll call you in a minute.

examples.en: It didn't rain, man, I'm telling you it didn't.

examples.es: Que sí, Hernando, que ya pago.
examples.en: Yes, Hernando, I told you, I'm paying now.

Que no, Mariana, que no vuelvo a Toronto.
examples.en: No, Mariana, I told you, I'm not going back to Toronto.

rule: Start with *que sí* or *que no*, as if you were finishing "I said…". Then add a name, and repeat with *que* plus the answer or the reason: *Que sí, mamá, que ya te llamo*. You can also close with the same word again: *que no*. The repeated *que* carries the "I told you", so you don't need to say it. Use it with people close to you. It sounds impatient, so with a stranger or a boss, don't.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a repeated *que* of insistence: *que* introduces something already said.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *sí* or *no* and type the whole sentence, to your mother who keeps asking: *Que ___, mamá, que ya te llamo.*
yourTurn.answer: Que sí, mamá, que ya te llamo.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Yes, Hernando, I told you, I'm paying now.
yourTurn.answer: Que sí, Hernando, que ya pago.
yourTurn.why: *Que sí* first, then a name, then *que* plus the news.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: No, Vale, I told you, I don't want any more.
yourTurn.answer: Que no, Vale, que no quiero más.
yourTurn.why: It starts with *que no*, and the second *que* brings the reason.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Yes, yes, I'm coming.
yourTurn.answer: Que sí, que sí, ya voy.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Que sí, que ya lo sé.* Say: No, I told you, I don't know.
yourTurn.answer: Que no, que no lo sé.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It didn't rain, man, I'm telling you it didn't.
yourTurn.answer: Que no llovió, hombre, que no.
yourTurn.why: Close with a bare *que no* for a firm ending.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: No, Mariana, I told you, I'm not going back to Toronto.
yourTurn.answer: Que no, Mariana, que no vuelvo a Toronto.
yourTurn.why: Same frame: *que no*, a name, *que no* plus the news.

pitfalls.why: Almost. You don't need to say "I said"; the bare *que* does that.

pitfalls.wrong: Que si, mamá, que ya te llamo.
pitfalls.right: Que sí, mamá, que ya te llamo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. This *sí* means "yes", so it needs its accent.

pitfalls.right: Ya le dije que no, señor.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Repeating *que no* sounds impatient, so with a stranger use *ya le dije*.

personal: Think of something you keep being asked. Answer it in one line with *Que sí* or *Que no*, and *que*.
